Q: How to make visual font size consistent across devices A:

In UX design we need to respect the user's preferences where we can. While you might want your interface to have a fixed size on all devices, Devices and users have reasons to why they scale fonts or resolutions. If you actively work against these features in this case by reversing their effects you may be harming those users.

S25 Ultra Users will have this issue with all of their apps, either they adapt and accept the default font size or they can change the font scaling settings in their device. Most S25 users will reconcile with this issue within the first day of ownership. On a device with font scaling enabled (Like my Grandma's) if your app fonts remain the normal size then users with impaired vision that need to scale fonts so they can read them will struggle to use your app and any others that do not respect the device settings.

If you deliberately want to prevent accessibility features from working within your app, then that's on you. But if this requirement comes purely out of testing your application across different devices and you noticed in screenshots that the fonts are different sizes, then you have made the wrong inference and should review if this is really a necessary requirement of your application.

It is acceptable to change your fonts based on responsive breakpoints, however be careful of manipulating fonts and layout based on system or browser level effects like font scaling or zoom factors. Depending on the nature of your application, limitations that restrict the user's ability to zoom or use accessibility features may end up excluding those members of the community from using your application.

Q: Faster command than "adb shell screencap"? A:

Old question, but you could try adb shell screencap screen.dump. This will skip the step to convert the file to png and will generate a file which can be read in Hex.

There are 12 bytes of header and then the file starts with the pixel colors at position (0,0) (top left) as RGBA.

The final size of the file depends on the size of your display.

Update 2026-Jan

That tip is usually helpful if the android device you are using is in an emulator running in your pc. In that case, you can still get the png, but you should do on your pc size, which is must faster and probably have better libraries. In that case, compressing the file (png or zip) won't give you any benefits as the transfer is usually much faster, and that is why this speeds up things so much. One last thing to keep in mind, if you don't mind the space, is using the lowest level of compression for png, for even less overhead. Here is the full command (using the newer exec-out):

  • exec-out: Pulls the raw binary stream
  • Skips the 12-byte Android header to get to pure pixels
  • magik: Receives raw RGBA data and converts to PNG at speed
adb exec-out screencap | tail -c +13 | \
 magick -depth 8 -size 1920x1080 rgba:- -quality 1 screenshot.png

Magik has some overhead, a slightly better solution using python, which can save you a few more millisecs:

adb exec-out screencap > /tmp/screen.raw

python3 -c "
import struct
from PIL import Image
data = open('/tmp/screen.raw', 'rb').read()
w, h, _ = struct.unpack('<III', data[:12])
Image.frombuffer('RGBA', (w, h), data[12:], 'raw', 'RGBA', 0, 1).save('screenshot.png', compress_level=1)
"

Q: How to create a temp table in Dbeaver from a csv file? A:

This is not specific to DBeaver, but to PostgreSQL. The way to create temporary tables in PostgreSQL with a SELECT query is:

CREATE TEMPORARY TABLE temptable AS
SELECT *
FROM mytable;

Q: Undefined reference to XML_GetErrorCode (and others) when building Apache A:

Try

yum install expat-devel

before installing Apache. I got this error when installing mod-wsgi-standalone on Amazon Linux, but maybe this solution also helps in the general case.
